name: Greece: participant-facing document QC
sources_note: Items without a source come from the QC checklist page; others name the page or file they come from.
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: Exact trial title, sponsor, EU trial number, protocol code and current protocol version are confirmed.
Correct Greek site, department, principal investigator and contact information.
Purpose and design stated in plain Greek without overstating efficacy or expected benefit.
Every treatment arm, randomisation, placebo or comparator and assignment probability described accurately.
Participant duration, visits, procedures and follow-up that change burden or risk are included.
Available alternatives outside the trial are explained.
Trial treatment distinguished from standard care; any post-trial treatment arrangements identified.

sections.title: Protocol-to-document consistency
sections.instruction: Compare with the protocol, IB, safety information, sample plan, data-flow description and insurance certificate.

items.check: Inclusion-relevant facts such as age, reproductive status and disease population match the protocol.
Doses, administration routes, visit schedules, invasive procedures and sample volumes match the protocol.
Risks reconciled with the current protocol, Investigator's Brochure and safety information.
Contraception methods, duration and pregnancy-testing requirements match the protocol.
Optional substudies are optional in both the protocol and the consent package.
Participant-facing endpoint questionnaires handled under Part I are not misplaced in Part II or omitted from the scientific dossier.
Voluntary participation and withdrawal are clear.
Adequate space for questions and decision time.
Main-trial consent is separate from optional future research, genetic testing or long-term sample storage.
What happens to data and samples after withdrawal is explained without promising actions that conflict with law or scientific integrity.
States when new information may lead to re-consent.
Confirms that the person receives a signed copy after consent.
The approved process matches Greece's in-person paper-consent guidance unless a different approach has been expressly accepted for the trial.

Each genuinely separable optional activity has its own clear choice recorded with a separate dated signature of the person consenting and the investigator (no YES/NO box or initials); refusal does not affect the main trial, treatment, ordinary care or reimbursement.

sections.title: Population and form coverage
sections.instruction: Map every inclusion pathway in the protocol to an information and consent set (see requirements.json population_sets).

items.check: Every inclusion pathway in the protocol maps to a population, populations are mutually exclusive within each consent stage, and every population has its full document set (see requirements.json population_sets).
The correct adult form is prepared for the ordinary pathway.
Healthy volunteers: disease-treatment assumptions removed and the absence of therapeutic intent explained.
Minors: age-appropriate information, written assent from age 10, and both-parent or guardian signatures.

Minors: protocol, CTIS age ranges and every document agree; the 10th and 18th birthday transitions are operationally defined; the form does not treat parental permission as a substitute for the child's information; refusal, dissent and withdrawal described without pressure.
Adults under court-appointed support: the participant's own information and expression of will plus the judicial supporter's consent.
Emergency enrolment: Article 35 eligibility documented and the prompt later-consent route described; participant and emergency-representative forms present.

Participants who cannot use the ordinary written route: the correct witness fields and procedure (one witness for deaf or unable to speak, two for unable to read or write, audio/video with one witness where approved).
Pregnancy follow-up: the pregnant person's permission is separate from later infant-data permission.
Optional future use: separate choices and withdrawal language.
Controller identified with contact details.
Data Protection Officer contact of the sponsor or applicable controller provided.
Each processing purpose and legal basis stated accurately.
Recipients or categories of recipients identified.
Transfers outside the European Economic Area and the safeguards used explained.
Retention period or the criteria used to set it stated.
Applicable access, correction, restriction, objection and complaint rights explained.
The Hellenic Data Protection Authority named as the national complaint authority.
Automated decision-making or profiling explained.
Privacy wording consistent with the sponsor's CTIS GDPR compliance statement (GR-R1).
Sample type, volume, collection schedule, storage location and planned retention described.
States whether samples are required for the main trial or optional.
Optional future research separated from main-study consent.
Scientific scope of future use and any transfer or sharing defined.
Coding, who can re-identify the sample, and when destruction or anonymisation is possible explained.
The Greek consent aligns with the CTIS biological-sample compliance template (GR-S1).
Every participant-facing version is in Greek.
A valid or certified translation exists for any expected participant who does not understand Greek.
No participant or public or private insurer is charged for trial-specific products, tests or procedures.
Insurance and injury-compensation information matches the certificate (GR-O1), including the pregnancy clause.
The document allows direct record access by authorised sponsor representatives and competent authorities while protecting confidentiality.
The National Ethics Committee contact is used correctly for ethics questions and is not described as the complaints authority.
Prohibited participant groups under the Greek implementing decision (compulsory military service, custodial sentence, barred by court decision, living in institutions) have not been included.
The blank submission form contains complete date fields for every signer.
The participant and investigator or authorised team member fields are present.
Both-parent fields appear for minors, subject to the documented national exceptions.
Legal-representative fields appear only for an applicable pathway.
One-witness or two-witness fields match the planned Greek procedure.
Pregnant-partner follow-up forms contain the nationally requested representative and two-witness fields.
Each page shows document type, protocol code or acronym, version and date.
Pagination is continuous and shows the total page count.
Clean and tracked-change versions are prepared for a modification.
CTIS publication versions have been checked for personal data and confidential information.

No drafting instruction remains in the final version (italic notes, [bracket] notes, ........... gaps, yellow [INSERT/IF/CHOOSE/NOTE] labels); fields completed by hand at consent stay blank; no participant, representative, witness or investigator signature in the blank CTIS copy.
Correct CTIS section and title per requirements.json (CTCG naming guide, _EL_el).
Plain, non-promotional Greek.
Abbreviations and medical terms explained.
Short sections, readable type and enough white space.
Risks presented by likelihood and seriousness where the evidence supports it.
Consent statements kept close to the signature page.
The final PDF is searchable, selectable and correctly rendered.
Translations reviewed by a qualified person and matching the approved source.
items.applies_when: document is adapted from a reference document in another language
